findings.summary: mutate() calls fn(stateFor(lift)) which still reads the stale outer `sets` closure, not the `s` parameter passed into the setSets updater — the exact same-batch clobbering bug the refactor claims to fix is still present.
findings.mechanism: stateFor(lift) is defined as `sets[keyFor(lift.id)] ?? seedFor(lift)`, referencing the outer-scope `sets` state variable captured in the closure, not the `s` argument of the `setSets(s => ...)` callback. When two taps on the same lift fire within one React batch, both invocations of the updater call fn(stateFor(lift)) against the same stale `sets` snapshot (the render-time value), so the second tap's mutation overwrites the first's instead of composing — identical to the pre-fix bug, just relocated inside the updater.

findings.summary: A side-effecting IndexedDB write (db.drafts.put) was moved inside the setSets functional updater, which React may invoke more than once per commit (e.g. StrictMode double-invoke, or bailout/re-render scenarios).
findings.mechanism: Functional state updaters are expected to be pure; performing an async DB write there means every extra invocation issues a redundant db.drafts.put call. The comment asserts this is harmless because the write is 'idempotent', but it still causes unnecessary duplicate writes/dexie transactions on every double-invocation, which wasn't a risk when the write lived outside the updater.
